ratings_why.fun: A moon you can see on the hero and wind yourself is easy to plan around, and Full Moons pay visible permanent growth; Borrow's hidden rules keep it from going higher.
ratings_why.distinct: A per-player phase clock plus borrowed text plays unlike any of today's tribes; Borrow itself echoes copy effects players know from other games.

verdict_why: Grandam of the Forms doesn't work as written, and Borrow's Full-moon condition reads differently across cards; both are small rewrites.

points.text: Grandam of the Forms fires on New Moon, but Borrow is only on while the moon is Full, so no Leveret is ever "borrowing a Hare" when she fires. Say "each Leveret becomes a copy of the Hare in front of it".

Borrow's Full-moon condition is hidden in the keyword: Ribboned Jack and the Leveret don't say Moonlit, Witch in Borrowed Shape does, and Sister Silverpenny opts out. That suggests Jack borrows all the time. Print "Moonlit: Borrow …" on every Borrower, and let Silverpenny's exception stand out.
The Borrow keyword is a paragraph of edge rules. Keep the card reminder to one line ("While Full, this also has that unit's text") and move the rest to a rules glossary.
Dame Waxwell reads more easily as "Your Full Moon and New Moon triggers fire twice, even Once a turn ones."
Waning has one card, Dusk Nurse. A Waning card would give the phase you pass through on the way to New a reason to show on the board.

standouts.why: Jill Longshanks boxing the enemy across is the seed's March boxing as a mechanic, and you can read the bout at a glance.
Old Wat, sold, turning the moon and always coming back is the character told in one line.
The Three Hares sharing their gains with neighbours is the church-roof icon turned into a clear rule.

weakest.why: Grandam of the Forms has the most text and the most hidden rules, and as written her trigger never finds a borrowing Leveret.
Dame Waxwell's Once-a-turn clause is clumsy to read.
Moon-Caller is clear but plain; its mid-fight Full is the hard part to follow on screen.

flags.note: New Moon trigger refers to Leverets "borrowing", which only happens under a Full moon.
Card text doesn't show that Borrow needs a Full moon, while Witch in Borrowed Shape's does.
Sister Silverpenny copies another tribe's best unit every turn from Tier 5.
Dame Waxwell with Mother Meikle Care stacks many Full Moon payouts per shop, and the log and animation have to keep them readable.
